name: GT-U7 GPS module
description: Goouuu Tech GT-U7 GPS receiver (u-blox 6 positioning engine, NEO-6M compatible) that streams NMEA sentences (position, altitude, speed, UTC time) over a UART at 9600 baud, once per second. The GT-U7 module itself runs on 2.7-3.6 V; the breakout's 3.3 V regulator lets it run from 3.3-5 V. Sold as: Goouuu Tech GT-U7 GPS module (MakerFocus and others; 5-pin header VCC, GND, RXD, TXD, PPS, micro-USB, IPEX antenna socket with patch antenna, backup battery, EEPROM), sold as a NEO-6M compatible GPS board.
eli5: Listens to GPS satellites and tells your board where on Earth it is, once a second.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V (on-board 3.3 V regulator feeds the 2.7-3.6 V GT-U7 module)

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Module serial input (3.3 V logic, 510 ohm series resistor on board): connect to the board's UART TX. Only needed to send configuration commands

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Module serial output, NMEA at 9600 baud 8N1: connect to the board's UART RX

pins.name: PPS
pins.description: Time pulse output (TIMEPULSE, 1 pulse per second once a fix is available); optional, for precise timing

buildNotes: Header order (component side, left to right): VCC, GND, RXD, TXD, PPS. The labels are printed on the back of the board.
Cross the serial lines: module TXD goes to the board's UART RX pin, module RXD (optional) to the board's UART TX pin.
Default is 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; open the UART at 9600 or the sentences come out as garbage.
The GT-U7's I/O pins are 3.3 V logic (absolute maximum 3.6 V). ESP32 and Pico are 3.3 V, so wire them directly; use a divider on RXD from 5 V logic.
Plug the patch antenna into the IPEX (U.FL) socket and give it a view of the sky. A cold start outdoors takes about 30 s or more; indoors it may never get a fix.
The LED on the board blinks once a second (driven by the time pulse) only when the module has a fix.
Peak supply current is about 67 mA during acquisition; power it from the board's 3V3 or 5V/VBUS pin, not a GPIO.

driver.code:
# Goouuu Tech GT-U7 GPS module (u-blox 6 positioning engine, NEO-6M compatible), MicroPython NMEA driver.
# The GT-U7 streams NMEA 0183 sentences (protocol 2.3) on its UART at 9600 baud, 8N1 by default,
# once per second. Each sentence is "$<talker><type>,<fields>*<cs>\r\n" where cs is the XOR of every
# character between '$' and '*' (u-blox 6 Receiver Description, NMEA protocol). GGA and RMC are decoded;
# latitude is ddmm.mmmmm and longitude dddmm.mmmmm (degrees + decimal minutes), S/W are negative.


def _checksum_ok(line):
    # line: str without CR/LF, starting with '$'
    star = line.rfind('*')
    if line[:1] != '$' or star < 0 or len(line) < star + 3:
        return False
    cs = 0
    for c in line[1:star]:
        cs ^= ord(c)
    try:
        return cs == int(line[star + 1:star + 3], 16)
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _deg(field, hemi, dlen):
    # 'ddmm.mmmmm' (dlen=2) or 'dddmm.mmmmm' (dlen=3) -> signed decimal degrees, None if empty
    if not field or not hemi:
        return None
    d = int(field[:dlen]) + float(field[dlen:]) / 60
    return -d if hemi in ('S', 'W') else d


def _num(field):
    return float(field) if field else None


class GTU7:
    def __init__(self, uart):
        """uart: machine.UART at 9600 baud whose rx pin is wired to the module's TXD."""
        self.uart = uart
        self._buf = b''
        self.fix = False          # GGA fix quality > 0, or RMC status 'A'
        self.fix_quality = 0      # GGA: 0 none, 1 GPS, 2 DGPS, 6 dead reckoning
        self.latitude = None      # decimal degrees, + north
        self.longitude = None     # decimal degrees, + east
        self.altitude = None      # metres above mean sea level (GGA)
        self.satellites = 0       # satellites used (GGA)
        self.hdop = None
        self.speed_knots = None   # speed over ground (RMC)
        self.course = None        # course over ground, degrees true (RMC)
        self.utc_time = None      # (hh, mm, ss)
        self.date = None          # (day, month, 2-digit year)
        self.bad_checksums = 0

    def update(self):
        """Read what has arrived and decode complete sentences. Returns True if a GGA or RMC was decoded."""
        n = self.uart.any()
        if n:
            data = self.uart.read(n)
            if data:
                self._buf += data
        got = False
        while True:
            nl = self._buf.find(b'\n')
            if nl < 0:
                break
            raw = self._buf[:nl].strip()
            self._buf = self._buf[nl + 1:]
            try:
                line = raw.decode()
            except UnicodeError:   # line noise / wrong baud rate
                self.bad_checksums += 1
                continue
            try:
                if line and self._parse(line):
                    got = True
            except (ValueError, IndexError):   # malformed field
                pass
        if len(self._buf) > 512:   # no newline for a long time: garbage, drop it
            self._buf = b''
        return got

    def _parse(self, line):
        if not _checksum_ok(line):
            self.bad_checksums += 1
            return False
        f = line[1:line.rfind('*')].split(',')
        kind = f[0][2:]   # skip the talker id (GP, GN, ...)
        if kind == 'GGA' and len(f) >= 10:
            self._time(f[1])
            self.fix_quality = int(f[6]) if f[6] else 0
            self.fix = self.fix_quality > 0
            self.satellites = int(f[7]) if f[7] else 0
            self.hdop = _num(f[8])
            if self.fix:
                self.latitude = _deg(f[2], f[3], 2)
                self.longitude = _deg(f[4], f[5], 3)
                self.altitude = _num(f[9])
            return True
        if kind == 'RMC' and len(f) >= 10:
            self._time(f[1])
            self.fix = f[2] == 'A'
            if self.fix:
                self.latitude = _deg(f[3], f[4], 2)
                self.longitude = _deg(f[5], f[6], 3)
                self.speed_knots = _num(f[7])
                self.course = _num(f[8])
            if len(f[9]) == 6:
                self.date = (int(f[9][0:2]), int(f[9][2:4]), int(f[9][4:6]))
            return True
        return False

    def _time(self, t):
        if len(t) >= 6:
            self.utc_time = (int(t[0:2]), int(t[2:4]), int(float(t[4:])))
